obligation: NERC CIP-008-6 R4 Reportable Cyber Security Incident notification
deadline: (High/medium impact BES Cyber Systems and associated EACMS) Within 1 hour after determination of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident; by end of next calendar day for an attempt to compromise an applicable system; updates within 7 calendar days of new information
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a NERC-registered entity and owns no BES Cyber Systems

obligation: Form DOE-417 Electric Emergency Incident and Disturbance Report (formerly OE-417; includes cyber events)
citation: Form DOE-417, OMB-approved ICR 202402-1901-002 (expires 2027-05-31); mandatory under 15 U.S.C. 772(b)
trigger: Electric utilities and other listed entities file when their Balancing Authority does not. Criteria 2-3 (Reportable Cyber Security Incident; cyber event interrupting operations) and 11-12 (cyber event that could affect reliability; loss of service to over 50,000 customers for 1 hour or more), among others
deadline: Within 1 hour (criteria 2-3), within 6 hours (criteria 11-12); final report within 72 hours
notify: DOE Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER)
applies_at_this_tier: No - no electric operations

obligation: TSA pipeline cybersecurity incident reporting
deadline: As soon as practicable, but no later than 72 hours after identifying a cybersecurity incident (IC Surface-2025-01 recommends earlier notice to TSA for significant incidents)
notify: CISA Central (cisa.gov/report or 844-729-2472); CISA shares with TSA
applies_at_this_tier: No for the consultant (not a TSA-designated Owner/Operator). Client A's own duty if its systems are affected; the consultant's 24-hour notice to Client A gives it the facts it needs to decide

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
deadline: 72 hours after reasonable belief a covered cyber incident occurred; 24 hours after ransom payment disbursed (proposed)
applies_at_this_tier: No - proposed only, not in effect (no final rule as of 2026-09-25). Under the proposal the consultant would also be below the SBA size standard for NAICS 541330 and is not a pipeline Owner/Operator reporting to TSA

obligation: State data breach notification
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - W-9 data (names and SSNs) of 5 subcontractors. All live in Florida today, so the Florida rows below apply; check each state's law if an affected person lives elsewhere

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Client A incident notice (contract)
citation: Client A Supplier Cybersecurity and Information Protection Addendum s.6
trigger: Any suspected security incident affecting Client A data, SSI, credentials, or portal access. Clock starts at discovery
deadline: Within 24 hours after discovery
notify: Client A security contact (24-hour line on the printed contact sheet)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - ransomware on the laptop always qualifies because the laptop holds Client A data and has had an open portal session

obligation: Client B incident notice (contract)
trigger: Suspected incident affecting Client B data
deadline: Within 72 hours after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Client B data was on the laptop or in synced folders

obligation: Client C notice (contract)
trigger: Suspected incident affecting Client C data
deadline: No set period; tell Client C without delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Client C data was on the laptop or in synced folders

obligation: Report of SSI released to unauthorized persons
trigger: The owner becomes aware that SSI has been released to unauthorized persons (for example, ransomware actors who took the SSI folder)
deadline: Promptly
notify: TSA, coordinated with Client A (SD 02G footnote 11 names SSI@tsa.dhs.gov as TSA's contact for SSI questions)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the laptop holds Client A SSI working copies

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information (name with SSN) of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. 15 more days only with good cause given in writing to the Department within 30 days (501.171(3)(a)); that extension covers only this individual notice
notify: Each affected subcontractor, by mail or email (501.171(4)(d))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - plan to the 30-day clock

obligation: Florida no-harm determination
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the owner reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if notice to individuals is not given; unlikely when SSNs are taken by criminals

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - 5 individuals

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: No - 5 individuals

obligation: Law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the business (inbound)
trigger: The accounting SaaS provider, which maintains personal information for the business, has a breach of its system
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determination
notify: The business (engineer-owner); the business then gives the notices above
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track the provider's notices

obligation: Subcontractor incident notice to the business (inbound)
trigger: A subcontractor's device or account holding client data is compromised or lost
deadline: Within 24 hours
applies_at_this_tier: Yes once terms are signed (POAM-007, due 2026-10-30)

obligation: Cyber insurance notice
deadline: As soon as practicable; call the breach hotline before hiring any outside firm
notify: Insurer breach hotline (panel counsel and forensics)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - $100,000 sublimit

obligation: Voluntary report to federal law enforcement
deadline: As soon as practical (supports the OFAC mitigation factor if payment is ever considered)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary
